quote: Hom(X,Y)=A(X×Y); Δ_X
body:
Take the explicit graded algebra \(A=\mathbf Q[t]/(t^2)\), \(\deg t=2\), with \(\kappa(1)=0\), \(\kappa(t)=1\), \(p_1^*x=x\otimes1\) and \((p_2)_*(x\otimes y)=\kappa(x)y\): the source's action sends \(u=a+b t_1+c t_2+d t_1t_2\) to
\[
\rho(u)(r+st)=(br+as)+(dr+cs)t,
\qquad \rho(u)=\begin{pmatrix}b&a\\d&c\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The inverse sends \(\begin{psmallmatrix}x&y\\z&w\end{psmallmatrix}\) to \(y+x t_1+w t_2+z t_1t_2\), and convolution against \(v=\alpha+\beta t_1+\gamma t_2+\delta t_1t_2\) has coefficients \((\beta a+\alpha c,\beta b+\alpha d,\delta a+\gamma c,\delta b+\gamma d)\), the coefficient vector obtained from \(\rho(v)\rho(u)\) by that displayed inverse map.
Consequently the explicit map takes \(t_1+t_2\) to the identity, \(t_1t_2\) to \(L=E_{21}\), \(1\) to \(\Lambda=E_{12}\), \(t_1\) to \(\pi_0=E_{11}\), and \(t_2\) to \(\pi_2=E_{22}\); the five-element \(n=1\) basis in CT16/017 therefore gives a map \(\Phi\otimes\mathbf Q\to\operatorname{End}(A)\) with \(\pi_1\mapsto0\) and kernel \(\mathbf Q\pi_1\), since the other four images are independent matrix units.
This is a fully specified single-object comparison for the planning question, with the multiplication checked directly and with no attribution of a general motive construction to the manuscript.

quote: il suffit de connaître δ_*; Δ=δ_*(1)
body:
For the same \(A=\mathbf Q[t]/(t^2)\) and trace, multiplication \(\mu:A\otimes A\to A\) has the explicit trace adjoint
\[
\delta_*(1)=\Delta=1\otimes t+t\otimes1,
\qquad \delta_*(t)=t\otimes t,
\qquad \delta_*(a)=(a\otimes1)\Delta.
\]
The basis products with \(b,c\in\{1,t\}\) verify \((\kappa\otimes\kappa)(\delta_*(a)(b\otimes c))=\kappa(abc)\), while \((t\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes t)\Delta=t\otimes t\), the flip fixes \(\Delta\), and \((\kappa\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\kappa)\Delta=1\).
Both iterates applied to 1 equal \(1\otimes t\otimes t+t\otimes1\otimes t+t\otimes t\otimes1\), and both applied to t equal \(t\otimes t\otimes t\), which checks coassociativity in this example.
These displayed maps give a concrete test for the unfinished diagonal axioms on 042 and explain the same diagonal element's unit action in O01, without asserting a complete general axiom list.

quote: on trouve une équivalence; spécial
body:
For each nonempty finite set I let P(I) be its set of partitions and \(B(I)=\mathbf Q^{P(I)}\), all in degree zero, with \(\kappa_I(x)=\sum_{p\in P(I)}x(p)\); for \(\alpha:I\to J\), pullback of partitions gives \(q_\alpha:P(J)\to P(I)\), and the bivariant map \(B(J)\to B(I)\) has algebra component \(q_\alpha^*\) and fiber-sum component \(q_{\alpha*}\).
The identities
\[
q_{\alpha*}(xq_\alpha^*y)=(q_{\alpha*}x)y,
\quad \kappa_Iq_{\alpha*}=\kappa_J,
\quad q_{\beta\alpha}=q_\alpha q_\beta
\]
give both projection formulas, gauge compatibility and contravariant functoriality, and the coordinate dot-product pairings are perfect, so these are Poincaré algebras in the written finite-projective sense of 027.
Let C be the constant \(\mathbf Q\) functor and t_I the indiscrete partition: the maps \(\tau_I^*(x)=x(t_I)\), \(\tau_{I*}(a)=a1_{\{t_I\}}\) form a natural bivariant transformation \(\tau:C\to B\), because \(q_\alpha(t_J)=t_I\), but its one-point component is the identity and its two-point component has rank one between dimensions one and two.
Thus evaluation at a point fails to reflect isomorphisms on the unrestricted category described in the ledger excerpt, whereas the source's special map here is \(\mathbf Q\otimes\mathbf Q\to\mathbf Q^2\), \(a\otimes b\mapsto(ab,ab)\), and is not an isomorphism, so this calculation tests the need to retain “spécial”; the retrieved appendix in MB13 expressly imposes the special condition and multiplicative gauges, so the present example lies outside that stated domain.

quote: produit fibré ... dim. correctes?; f_*(y)=yσ
body:
Write \(\mathbf Q_\lambda\) for the degree-zero algebra Q with trace \(\lambda\operatorname{id}\): the pair \((f^*,f_*)=(\operatorname{id},(\lambda/\mu)\operatorname{id})\) is an actual bivariant isomorphism \(\mathbf Q_\lambda\to\mathbf Q_\mu\), with inverse ratio \(\mu/\lambda\).
Use the square \(X'\xrightarrow{q}X\), \(Y'\xrightarrow{p}Y\), with vertical maps \(f':X'\to Y'\), \(f:X\to Y\), where \(X'=\mathbf Q_2\) and \(X=Y'=Y=\mathbf Q_1\): all pullbacks are identities, \(q_*=f'_*=2\operatorname{id}\), \(f_*=p_*=\operatorname{id}\), the square commutes, and its universal lift is \(h=q^{-1}u\) with \(f'h=p^{-1}fu=v\), proving that it is Cartesian.
All four assigned degrees are zero, yet
\[
p^*f_*=\operatorname{id}\ne2\operatorname{id}=f'_*q^*,
\qquad f^*p_*=\operatorname{id}\ne2\operatorname{id}=q_*f'^*.
\]
This is a concrete negative answer to the literal abstract sufficiency question in the gauge category and uses exactly the \(\sigma=2\) mechanism of 042; it does not transfer that conclusion to a geometric cohomology square with its specified trace normalizations.

\[
f_*(x f^*y)=(-1)^{ij}f_*(f^*y\,x)
=(-1)^{ij}y f_*x
=(-1)^{ij+j(i+\delta)}f_*x\,y
=(-1)^{\delta j}f_*x\,y.
\]
This reproduces the exact exponent written in the margin on 034 and explains the disappearance of this factor under the even-degree restriction explicitly adopted on 031.

CT47/003 writes \(\Phi_{\mathcal L}(F)=\mathbf R p_{2*}(\mathbf Lp_1^*F\otimes\mathcal L)\), and taking its recorded K-class gives the actual comparison map
\[
[F]\longmapsto[\Phi_{\mathcal L}(F)]
=p_{2*}\bigl([\mathcal L]\,p_1^*[F]\bigr).
\]
This is the same pullback–kernel product–pushforward operator pattern displayed on 011, with the kernel identified explicitly as \([\mathcal L]\), and CT47/004 supplies the corresponding base-change, projection and Künneth calculation for its product assertion.
The comparison is through this written K-class map and its operations; no equivalence between a derived category and the general correspondence category is asserted.
